pull.title: [DONTMERGE] Test run with reproducer for forced chunked send
pull.body:
WARNING: NOT INTENDED FOR MERGING!

Performing a test run with forced chunked send. 

All networking code using sockets must not make assumption about the chunking of the incoming/outgoing data, and should be resilient against any chunking. Normally, the chunking of the sends of the writer dictate the chunking of the receives at the reader, but this is not guaranteed by IP/TCP, intermediate networking elements may change the packet structure.

This branch contains a stress test reproducer. For every socket send, sending is changed to break up data in small chunks. This forcedly changes chunking of the data stream. The goal is to test code for robustness in face of unexpected chunking of the data.

This PR will be closed once the test runs complete, and kept for reference (some tests are expected to fail).

test: interface_http: Fix for case when a response doesn't arrive in one recv

Several checks read a response with one recv() call (recv_raw(), up to
1024 bytes) and assumed it held the whole HTTP response. TCP does not
guarantee this: on a slow or loaded machine a response can arrive split
across several reads, so the check sees only the status line or headers
and fails.

The loops in check_pipelining and check_slow_read_throttle had a related
problem. They counted "HTTP/1.1 200" markers in each read separately, so
a marker split across two reads was never counted, and the loop waited
until the socket timed out.

Add BitcoinHTTPConnection.recv_responses(count), which keeps reading
until `count` complete responses (headers plus Content-Length body) have
arrived, or the server closes the connection. Use it everywhere a full
response is expected, and replace the counting loops with explicit
assertions on the result.

recv_raw() is kept for the timeout checks, where a single blocking read
is the intended behaviour.

test: p2p: check v1 magic bytes only after the full header

The v1 message parser in P2PConnection rejected the stream as soon as
the first 4 bytes did not match the network magic. bitcoind's
V1Transport::readHeader waits for the full 24-byte header before
checking the magic.

The v2 to v1 downgrade relies on bitcoind's behaviour: an outbound v2
connection is only retried with v1 (V2Transport::ShouldReconnectV1)
if at least a v1 header's worth of bytes had been sent before the
peer disconnected. If the node's first send reaches the test peer in
small pieces, the Python peer could disconnect after just 4 bytes, the
node would not retry with v1, and p2p_v2_encrypted.py would time out
waiting for the reconnection.

Match bitcoind by checking the magic only once the full header has
been received.

test: p2p_v2_misbehaving: Handle partial ellswift read

The node's 64-byte ellswift key can arrive in several chunks. In that
case EncryptedP2PState.complete_handshake() returns (0, b"") to signal
that more data is needed. The WrongGarbageTerminatorState override
bit-flipped the returned bytes unconditionally, which crashed in
random_bitflip() on empty input and dropped the connection.

Return the "need more data" result unchanged before tampering with it.
